Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:3:Serena uses a project-based workflow.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:4:A **project** is simply a directory on your filesystem that contains code and other files
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:7:Assuming that you have project you want to work with (which may initially be empty),
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:8:setting up a project with Serena typically involves the following steps:
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:10:1. **Project creation**: Configuring project settings for Serena (and indexing the project, if desired)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:11:2. **Project activation**: Making Serena aware of the project you want to work with
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:12:3. **Onboarding**: Getting Serena familiar with the project (creating memories)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:13:4. **Working on coding tasks**: Using Serena to help you with actual coding tasks in the project
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:15:(project-creation-indexing)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:18:Project creation is the process of defining fundamental project settings that are relevant to Serena's operation.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:20:You can create a project either  
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:21: * explicitly, using the project creation command (see below), or
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:22: * implicitly, by just activating a directory as a project while already in a conversation; this will use default settings for your project (skip to the next section).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:26:To explicitly create a project, use the following command while in the project directory:
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:28:    serena project create [options] [project directory]
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:30: * The project directory defaults to the current directory if not specified.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:31: * For an existing project, the programming languages will be detected based on
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:32:   the source files present, and the main language will be activated automatically.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:34: * For an empty project, you can optionally specify one or more languages
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:35:   to be activated explicitly via the `--language` parameter
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:37: * You can optionally specify a custom project name with `--name my-name`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:38: * You can immediately index the project after creation with `--index`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:40:(project-config)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:43:After creation, you can adjust the project settings in the generated `.serena/project.yml` file
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:44:within the project directory.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:46:The file allows you to configure ...
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:47:  * the name by which you want to refer to the project (relevant when telling the LLM to dynamically activate the project)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:48:  * the set of programming languages for which language servers are spawned (not relevant when using the JetBrains plugin)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:49:    Note that you can dynamically add/remove language servers while Serena is running via the [Dashboard](060_dashboard).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:50:  * the [language backend](per-project-language-backend) to use for this project (overriding the global setting)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:55:  * an initial prompt that shall be passed to the LLM whenever the project is activated
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:56:  * the set of tools and modes to use for the project
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:60:[template file](https://github.com/oraios/serena/blob/main/src/serena/resources/project.template.yml).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:63:Many settings in project.yml *extend* or *override* settings in the global configuration file `serena_config.yml`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:64:So use the project configuration specifically for aspects that apply only to the particular project.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:67:**Local Overrides**. The project.yml file is intended to be versioned together with the project.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:68:You can specify local overrides for the settings in a `project.local.yml` file in the same directory
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:70:Any keys defined therein will override the respective key in `project.yml`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:75:In monorepos or multi-package setups, Serena's language server normally only sees symbols within the
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:76:project root. To enable cross-package references (e.g. `find_referencing_symbols` discovering usages
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:77:in sibling packages), configure `additional_workspace_folders` in your `project.yml`:
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:86:Paths can be absolute or relative to the project root. Each folder is registered as an LSP workspace
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:87:folder, and the language server will discover symbols and references across all listed packages.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:89:**Currently supported for:** TypeScript. Other language servers will raise an error if this setting
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:91:`_find_representative_source_file()` method in the respective language server class.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:94:Each additional workspace folder adds startup time, as the language server needs to index the
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:95:additional projects. For large monorepos, consider listing only the packages you actively need
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:106:Especially for larger project, it can be advisable to index the project after creation, pre-caching 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:107:symbol information provided by the language server(s). This will avoid delays during the first tool invocation
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:108:that requires symbol information.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:110:While in the project directory, run this command:
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:112:    <serena> project index
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:116:(project-activation)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:119:Project activation makes Serena aware of the project you want to work with.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:121: * while in a conversation, by telling the LLM to activate a project, e.g.,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:123:      * "Activate the project /path/to/my_project" (for first-time activation with auto-creation)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:124:      * "Activate the project my_project"
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:126:   Note that this option requires the `activate_project` tool to be active, 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:127:   which it isn't in single-project [contexts](contexts) like `ide` or `claude-code` *if* a project is provided at startup.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:128:   (The tool is deactivated, because we assume that in these contexts, user will only work on the single, open project and have
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:131: * when the MCP server starts, by passing the project path or name as a command-line argument
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:132:   (e.g. when using a single-project mode like `ide` or `claude-code`): `--project <path|name>`
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:134:When working with the JetBrains plugin, be sure to have the same project folder open as a project in your IDE,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:135:i.e. the folder that is activated in Serena should correspond to the root folder of the project in your IDE.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:139:By default, Serena will perform an **onboarding process** when
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:140:it is started for the first time for a project.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:141:The goal of the onboarding is for Serena to get familiar with the project
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:142:and to store memories, which it can then draw upon in future interactions.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:144:In general, **memories** provide a way for Serena to store and retrieve 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:145:information about the project, relevant conventions, and other relevant aspects.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:148:or disable these features, see [Memories & Onboarding](045_memories).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:153:When using Serena to work on your project, it can be helpful to follow a few best practices.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:175:set `git config core.autocrlf` to `true` on Windows.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:176:With `git config core.autocrlf` set to `false` on Windows, you may end up with huge diffs
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:181:git config --global core.autocrlf true
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:197:There are several ways in which you might want to work with multiple projects simultaneously.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:201:If fulfilling a task requires a single agent to edit code in multiple projects, the recommended approach is to create a **monorepo folder**,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:202:i.e. a folder that contains all the projects as sub-folders, and open that monorepo folder as a project in Serena.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:203:You may also use symbolic links to create a monorepo folder if the projects are located in different places on your filesystem.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:205:If several languages are used across the projects, specify all of them as needed when using the LSP backend;
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:206:For JetBrains mode, make sure that your IDE is configured to work with all the languages used across the projects (e.g. by installing the respective language plugins).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:208:(query-projects)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:211:If, while working on a project, you want Serena to be able to read code or other information from another project (e.g. a library or otherwise related project), 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:212:this can be enabled via the `query_project` tool.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:213:Provided that the project you want to query is known to Serena (i.e. you have created it as described above),
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:214:the `query_project` tool allows the agent to query files and symbolic information from that project.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:216:To enable this tool, [activate the mode](modes) `query-projects`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:217:This also enables a second tool for listing projects that can be queried.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:219:Depending on the language backend being used, the management of resources for the external projects varies:
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:221:* When using the JetBrains backend, make sure that every project for which you want symbolic queries to work is open in an IDE instance. 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:222:* When using the LSP backend, executing symbolic tools via the query tool requires that Serena's **Project Server** be started,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:223:  which will automatically spawn the necessary language servers for the projects that are queried.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:227:      serena start-project-server
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:232:If you want multiple agents to access the same project via a single Serena instance,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:233:i.e. you do not want several instances of Serena (including its language servers) to be running,

Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:240:For this use case, simply run a separate instance of Serena for each project, which naturally
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\040_workflow.md:241:occurs when Serena is started by the MCP client in stdio mode.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:13:  * **project-specific memories**, which are stored in the `.serena/memories/` directory within your project folder, and
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:14:  * **global memories**, which are shared across all projects and, by default, are stored in `~/.serena/memories/global/`
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:16:The LLM is informed about the existence of memories and instructed to read them when appropriate, 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:18:When the agent starts working on a project, it receives the list of available memories. 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:19:The agent should be instructed to update memories by the user when appropriate.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:25:The `list_memories` tool can filter by topic, allowing the agent to explore even large numbers of memories in a structured way.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:27:(global-memories)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:30:Global memories use the top-level topic `global`, i.e. whenever a memory name starts with `global/`, 
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:31:it is stored in the global memories directory and is shared across all projects.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:33:By default, deletion and editing of global memories is allowed.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:36:project-level [configuration](050_configuration). For example, setting "global/.*" will mark all global memories as read-only. The agent will be informed which memories are read-only.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:38:Since global memories are not versioned alongside your project files,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:39:it can be helpful to track global memories with git (i.e. to make `~/.serena/memories/` a git repository)
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:45:to exclude them from `list_memories` and `activate_project` output. Add regex patterns to the
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:46:global or project-level [configuration](050_configuration):
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:52:Ignored memories are completely excluded — they cannot be accessed via `read_memory`, `write_memory`,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:53:or any other memory tool. To read an ignored memory file, use the `read_file` tool on the raw file path
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:54:(e.g., `.serena/memories/_archive/2026-03/some-topic.md`).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:56:Like `read_only_memory_patterns`, patterns from the global and project-level configurations are merged additively.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:60:You may edit memories directly in the file system, using your preferred text editor or IDE.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:61:Alternatively, access them via the [Serena Dashboard](060_dashboard), which provides a graphical interface for
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:62:viewing, creating, editing, and deleting memories while Serena is running.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:64:(onboarding)=
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:67:By default, Serena performs an **onboarding process** when it encounters a project
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:68:for the first time (i.e., when no project memories exist yet).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:69:The goal of the onboarding is for Serena to get familiar with the project —
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:71:and to store this knowledge as memories for future interactions.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:73:In further project activations, Serena will check whether onboarding was already
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:74:performed by looking for existing project memories and will skip the onboarding
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:75:process if memories are found.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:79:1. When a project is activated, Serena checks whether onboarding was already
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:80:   performed (by checking if any memories exist).
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\045_memories.md:81:2. If no memories are found, Serena triggers the onboarding process, which

Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:3:In this section we describe the methodology we applied in evaluating the performance of Serena's tools.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:5:The evaluation measures the **concrete delta** that Serena's tools provide on top of an agent's
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:14:1. **Generality.** The evaluation mechanism should be broadly applicable and repeatable by any user, on any project, with any agent.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:18:   install, configure, or script beyond what you already have.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:24:   tools, so it is in the best position to judge whether a semantic tool improves its workflow
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:27:   problem of a human evaluator having to simulate how an agent would use the tools — the agent
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:34:   from the codebase at hand, performs each task using both toolsets side by side, and classifies
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:44:1. **Codebase understanding** — structural overviews, targeted symbol retrieval, reference finding, type hierarchies, and external dependency lookup.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:46:3. **Multi-file changes** — cross-file renames, symbol and file moves, safe deletes, and inlining.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:50:For every task, the agent executes the full end-to-end workflow using **both** toolsets (Serena's semantic
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:51:tools and its own built-in tools), applies real edits verified via `git diff`, and records call counts,
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:72:tasks using both toolsets, record concrete measurements (call counts, payload sizes, prerequisite
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:74:neutral and negative deltas honestly — the Claude Code report explicitly notes that small edits are
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:84:that the findings reflect genuine properties of the toolset rather than artefacts of a particular
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:90:  tools, so it can report on workflow friction, payload overhead, and call counts from first-hand
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:94:  what the project actually contains (e.g. skipping inline if no suitable candidate exists, as the
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\010_methodology.md:95:  Claude Code report did for Python, while the Codex report found a suitable Java candidate).

Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\050_configuration.md:324:**Why this exists**: clojure-lsp discovers source paths only from the project descriptor at the workspace root (root `deps.edn` / `project.clj` / `shadow-cljs.edn` / `bb.edn`) and does not recurse for sub-module descriptors. In multi-module monorepos (e.g. `common/` + `frontend/` + `backend/` layouts), this means references in sibling modules are silently missed by `find_referencing_symbols` until a tool call happens to open one of their files. Serena works around this by walking the repo for project descriptors at startup and passing the union of their declared source paths to clojure-lsp via `initializationOptions["source-paths"]`.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\050_configuration.md:329:2. `config_edn_path` setting — Serena parses `:source-paths` from the supplied file.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\050_configuration.md:330:3. `<repo>/.lsp/config.edn` exists — Serena injects nothing; clojure-lsp reads the file natively, so hand-tuned project configs are never clobbered.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\02-usage\050_configuration.md:331:4. Walk the repo for project descriptors and synthesise a source-paths list from their declared `:paths` / `:extra-paths` / `:source-paths` (skipping `.git`, `.clj-kondo`, `.lsp`, `.cpcache`, `node_modules`, `target`, `out`, `dist`).

Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:47:**2. Structural overview / targeted symbol reading (Serena: moderate positive)**
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:48:- `get_symbols_overview(depth=1)`: 1 call returns all classes, methods, and attributes in structured JSON, via the IDE's parser — language-agnostic and always correct. Built-in equivalent: `Grep` for a language-specific heuristic pattern like `^(class |def )`. This works for simple Python files but is inherently fragile: the pattern must be hand-tuned per language, misses decorated or multi-line declarations, and can match inside strings or comments. For non-Python languages, an entirely different regex would be needed.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:49:- `find_symbol(include_body=True)`: Retrieves a specific method body by name path without reading surrounding code. Built-in: requires knowing the line number (via Grep) then Read with offset — 2 calls.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:53:- `find_referencing_symbols`: Returns which *symbols* reference a target, with file grouping and usage type (import, call, type annotation). Built-in `Grep` returns all text matches including docs, comments, and string literals — same recall but lower precision.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:54:- Frequency: Moderate. Value per hit: Moderate — precision matters when planning refactors of widely-used symbols.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:61:- Serena addresses symbols by name path (`CollectStats/refresh_return_stats`), which is invariant under edits elsewhere in the file. The built-in workflow is fundamentally line-number-mediated: Grep returns line numbers, Read takes line offsets — and both go stale after any edit to the file. Edit's text matching (`old_string`) is more resilient than line numbers, but it sits at the end of a chain that starts with position-based lookups. After an edit shifts lines, previously noted Grep results and Read offsets are invalid and must be re-acquired.
Z:/repos/deps/serena/docs\04-evaluation\030_results\010_cc_on_tianshou.md:66:- For a 1-line change inside a 13-line method, Serena's `replace_symbol_body` requires sending the entire 13-line body. Edit sends just the changed line. The prerequisite cost differs: Serena needs `find_symbol(include_body=True)` to get the body; Edit needs `Read` of the relevant lines. Both are 1 prerequisite call + 1 edit call.

prompt\nhooks.\n\n## What Changed\n\n- Added `PreCompact` and `PostCompact` hook events across hook config,\ndiscovery, dispatch, generated schemas, app-server notifications,\nanalytics, and TUI hook rendering.\n- Added trigger matching for compact hooks with the documented `manual`\nand `auto` matcher values.\n- Wired `PreCompact` before both local and remote compaction, and\n`PostCompact` after successful local or remote compaction.\n- Kept compact hook command input to lifecycle metadata: session id,\nCodex turn id, transcript path, cwd, hook event name, model, and\ntrigger.\n- Made compact stdout handling consistent with other hooks: plain stdout\nis ignored as debug output, while malformed JSON-looking stdout is\nreported as failed hook output.\n- Added integration coverage for compact hook dispatch, trigger\nmatching, post-compact execution, and the audited behavior that\n`decision:\"block\"` does not block compaction.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Hook-specific compaction blocking is not implemented;\n`decision:\"block\"` and exit-code-2 blocking semantics are intentionally\nunsupported for `PreCompact`.\n- Custom compaction instructions are not exposed to compact hooks in\nthis PR.\n- Compact summaries, summary character counts, and summary previews are\nnot exposed to compact hooks in this PR.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo test -p codex-hooks`\n- `cargo test -p codex-core\nmanual_pre_compact_block_decision_does_not_block_compaction`\n- `cargo test -p codex-app-server hooks_list`\n- `cargo test -p codex-core config_schema_matches_fixture`\n- `cargo test -p codex-tui hooks_browser`\n\n## Docs\n\nThe developer documentation for Codex hooks should be updated alongside\nthis feature to document `PreCompact` and `PostCompact`, the\n`manual`/`auto` matcher 416: 
417: ## 9. Practical Usage Rule
418: 
419: **Use Serena for:** Any cross-file refactoring (rename, move), any "who uses this?" query, any type-hierarchy navigation, any full-method-body replacement, and any situation where you need symbol-accurate results without false positives.
420: 
421: **Use built-ins for:** Small edits (1–3 lines) inside methods, free-text search, reading non-code files, file discovery, and shell operations.
422: 
423: **Hybrid pattern (most efficient):** Use Serena to explore (overview, find symbol, find references) and Edit for small targeted changes. Use Serena for any cross-file refactoring. Use `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` for non-code tasks and text search. This combination captures the strengths of both toolsets.
424: 
425: **Verdict:** The optimal workflow uses Serena's semantic tools for code navigation and cross-file refactoring, and built-in Edit for small single-file changes. The two toolsets are complementary — Serena handles the structured code operations, built-ins handle the text and system operations.

Usage: repomix [options] [directories...]

Repomix - Pack your repository into a single AI-friendly file

Arguments:
  directories                         list of directories to process (default:
                                      ["."])

Basic Options
  -v, --version                       Show version information and exit

CLI Input/Output Options
  --verbose                           Enable detailed debug logging (shows file
                                      processing, token counts, and
                                      configuration details)
  --quiet                             Suppress all console output except errors
                                      (useful for scripting)
  --stdout                            Write packed output directly to stdout
                                      instead of a file (suppresses all logging)
  --stdin                             Read file paths from stdin, one per line
                                      (specified files are processed directly)
  --copy                              Copy the generated output to system
                                      clipboard after processing
  --token-count-tree [threshold]      Show file tree with token counts; optional
                                      threshold to show only files with ≥N
                                      tokens (e.g., --token-count-tree 100)
  --top-files-len <number>            Number of largest files to show in summary
                                      (default: 5, e.g., --top-files-len 20)

Repomix Output Options
  -o, --output <file>                 Output file path (default:
                                      repomix-output.xml, use "-" for stdout)
  --style <type>                      Output format: xml, markdown, json, or
                                      plain (default: xml)
  --parsable-style                    Escape special characters to ensure valid
                                      XML/Markdown (needed when output contains
                                      code that breaks formatting)
  --compress                          Extract essential code structure (classes,
                                      functions, interfaces) using Tree-sitter
                                      parsing
  --output-show-line-numbers          Prefix each line with its line number in
                                      the output
  --no-file-summary                   Omit the file summary section from output
  --no-directory-structure            Omit the directory tree visualization from
                                      output
  --no-files                          Generate metadata only without file
                                      contents (useful for repository analysis)
  --remove-comments                   Strip all code comments before packing
  --remove-empty-lines                Remove blank lines from all files
  --truncate-base64                   Truncate long base64 data strings to
                                      reduce output size
  --header-text <text>                Custom text to include at the beginning of
                                      the output
  --instruction-file-path <path>      Path to file containing custom
                                      instructions to include in output
  --split-output <size>               Split output into multiple numbered files
                                      (e.g., repomix-output.1.xml,
                                      repomix-output.2.xml); size like 500kb,
                                      2mb, or 2.5mb
  --include-empty-directories         Include folders with no files in directory
                                      structure
  --include-full-directory-structure  Show entire repository tree in the
                                      Directory Structure section, even when
                                      using --include patterns
  --no-git-sort-by-changes            Don't sort files by git change frequency
                                      (default: most changed files first)
  --include-diffs                     Add git diff section showing working tree
                                      and staged changes
  --include-logs                      Add git commit history with messages and
                                      changed files
  --include-logs-count <count>        Number of recent commits to include with
                                      --include-logs (default: 50)

File Selection Options
  --include <patterns>                Include only files matching these glob
                                      patterns (comma-separated, e.g.,

  -i, --ignore <patterns>             Additional patterns to exclude

  --no-gitignore                      Don't use .gitignore rules for filtering
                                      files
  --no-dot-ignore                     Don't use .ignore rules for filtering
                                      files
  --no-default-patterns               Don't apply built-in ignore patterns
                                      (node_modules, .git, build dirs, etc.)

Remote Repository Options
  --remote <url>                      Clone and pack a remote repository (GitHub

Configuration Options
